column2: “Then just one more run.”
Giving in to {n2}'s pleading look, I reluctantly agreed.
“That's the spirit!”
{n2} cheerfully glided off toward the lift.
Maybe I should have flatly refused...
Trailing clumsily after her, I was already starting to regret it.
When we got to the top, {n2} came out with something outrageous.
“Since it's the last run, let's go up a bit higher.”
“Whaaat?!”
“Come on?
You're bored of the beginner course too, right?”
“But I can't even do a proper snowplow {C3}(ski braking technique){C0} yet...”
“It's fine.
If you think you can't do it, just fall.”
“...I'll pass.{r}{p}You can go by yourself.{r}{p}I'd only be slow anyway.”
“Really?
...Sorry, then. Wait for me, okay?”
{n2} glided off toward the lift with an embarrassed smile.
Following {n2}'s ski wear with my eyes as she rode the lift up, I noticed the weather was starting to look bad.
Standing still, I was getting colder and colder, and my sweat-soaked underwear felt ready to freeze.
Better to get home early...
As I was thinking that, {n2} came skiing down the slope in front of me.
“That was fast.”
I said in surprise, and she shrugged.
“This is normal.{r}{p}Well, shall we head back?”{g}
We got into the 4WD borrowed from {n2}'s uncle, Mr. Kobayashi.
“...Okay.
Let's go.”
I hated the thought of being seen as scared, so I decided to take the challenge.
By the time we went up one more level, the sun had dimmed and few people were left on the slopes.
It felt like the wind had suddenly turned colder, too.
From below, it had looked like a slope that was nothing special...
But now that I'd come up by lift, there was no way I thought I could ski down alone.
Couldn't I find some excuse to ride the lift back down?
Like saying I'd sprained my ankle, or that my bindings were acting up...
“Ready?
Okay, here we go.”
{n2} seemed unaware of my inner thoughts.
“An intermediate course...
maybe it's still too soon.”
It was quite a struggle to keep her from noticing my voice shaking.
“What are you saying?
It's fine, it's fine.{r}{p}You've been training since morning, so you can handle this much.”
{n2} laughed and gave my back a hard shove.
wha...
whaaa...”
My body began to slide forward, swoosh.{r}{p}Before I could stop with my poles, I shot out onto the steep slope.
“Put your weight forward!”
I could hear {n2}'s voice, but I had no time for that.
My skis were going faster and faster on their own.
Less like sliding than falling, I picked up speed and kept picking it up.
{n2} pulled up beside me and called out.
“Don't forget your snowplow!
Slow down more!”
I know.
My head knows.
But my body wouldn't move the way I wanted.
I was skiing as if flying through the air.
Turning was out of the question.
“Waaaaaaah!”
I fell on purpose, but I'd built up too much speed.
I tumbled down the slope and came to a stop covered in snow.
“Are you okay?”
{n2}'s skis kicked up the snow in front of me and stopped.
“Oh, yeah.
It's nothing.”
Putting on a brave front, I put both hands down and tried to stand up, but...
“Ow, ow, ow!”
Sharp pain shot through my left ankle.
Looking, I saw the right ski had come off my boot cleanly, but the left ski had stubbornly stayed on.
Because of that, it seemed only my left foot had been badly twisted.
“Stay still.”
{n2} knelt, took off my boot, and gently examined my ankle.
“I don't think it's broken, but...
we're still close, so it's safer to go back to the lift.”
“Sorry.”
“No.
I forced you to come, so I'm the one who should apologize.”
Somehow getting up with {n2}'s shoulder to lean on, the ski patrol rushed over right away.
At the first-aid room, luckily it was just a sprain.
After a compress as first aid, we left the slopes.
By the time we reached the parking lot it was completely dark, and what's more, snow had begun to fall.
“Can you
drive?”
{n2} asked, worried.
“...Looks like not really.{r}{p}{n2},
you have a license, right?”
“Yeah...
technically.”
Her answer sounded oddly unsure, but it couldn't be helped.
We strapped the skis onto the 4WD's roof, and I got into the passenger seat while {n2} got in the driver's seat.
Just to be extra safe, we buckled our seat belts tightly.
The engine started.
We waited for it to warm up, then slowly pulled out.
Looking at her, she was stiff with tension.
I'm uneasy...
just drive calmly and you'll be fine...”
“Don't talk to me right now!”
I'm very uneasy...
The farther we got from the slopes, the worse the snow got, and the streetlights disappeared.
No matter how the wipers swept, snow kept sticking to the windshield one flake after another.
On both sides, piled-up snow and deep woods.
It was pitch dark already.
On the way here it had been light and not snowing, so it took only about fifteen minutes.
But at this rate, the return trip might take twice as long.
{n2} drove clinging to the steering wheel, glaring at the outside.
“Ah!”
Suddenly something crossed the headlights, and {n2} slammed on the brakes.
Then she jerked the wheel, and the car left the road and plowed into a mound of snow.
The seat belt dug into my shoulder and I stopped breathing for a moment.
For a while neither of us could speak.
“I'm sorry...
but what was that just now?”
“A weasel or something.{r}{p}More importantly...
does the car still run?”
The engine had stalled.
{n2} hurriedly tried to start the engine.
But no matter how many times she tried, it wouldn't start.
“Oh no...”
I couldn't help saying it aloud.
“What do we do...?”
{n2} looked ready to cry.
I mustn't show my anxiety here.
Thinking that, I deliberately spoke in a cheerful voice.
“No help for it.
Let's walk.{r}{p}There might be a house along the way, and someone might pass by in a car.”
“Wouldn't it be better to stay here?{r}{p}In this snow we might get lost, and even if not, we could freeze to death.”
“If the engine won't start, we'll freeze to death here too.”
{n2} bit her lip.
But as the inside of the car gradually grew cold, she seemed to understand that my opinion was right.
“You're right...
then let's set out as soon as possible.”
Putting on the ski gloves we'd taken off and closing our collars tightly, we got out of the car.
Luckily, the car had a powerful flashlight on board, probably for situations like this.
Outside, a blizzard slashing in at an angle attacked us.
{n2} and I naturally held hands and started walking.
The circle lit by the flashlight was far too feeble and small.
The shrill wind shook the surrounding trees and froze my bare nose and ears.
The freezing air brought a piercing pain not only to my nasal membranes but deep into my lungs.
My ankle felt hot, but the pain wasn't enough to keep me from walking.
“Where
are we?”
{n2} asked, wheezing.
“Huh?
Don't you know better than me?”
“It's my first time driving around here myself...”
“Sounds good.”
Fed and rested, I felt up to one more run.
“Then let's go.”
“Better not today.”
Midori, who was clearing away dishes, cut in from the side.
“From the weather forecast I heard, forget night skiing.{r}{p}Looks safest not to go out of here for a while.”
“Is it really that bad?”
The one who answered was the other part-timer, Toshio Kubota.
“The forecast says it might be the heaviest snowfall in years.”
“It's fine, it's fine.
Don't worry.”
{n2} was raring to go.
I hesitated a little, then said:
“Let's not, after all.”
“You think so...?”
“We're tired from the day, and it's an accident waiting to happen...”
“You're right...
that's the wiser choice.”
Even as she said that, {n2} seemed a little disappointed.
Just then, a commotion reached us from the hall, and {n2} and I took the opportunity to leave the dining room.
“Okay, let's go!”
We changed back into our ski wear and set out, borrowing Mr. Kobayashi's car.
The snow and wind were a bit stronger, but inside the heated car it didn't bother me at all.
The studless-tired 4WD plowed ahead undaunted through the snowy night road.
About fifteen minutes after leaving the inn, something suddenly crossed the headlights.
“Whoa!”
I hurriedly turned the wheel left.
With a nasty scraping sound, the body rubbed the guardrail.
With a violent impact, the world spun around.
...When I came to, I was lying in pitch darkness in an unnatural position.
My face felt slimy somehow.
I tried to touch it and realized I couldn't move my hands freely.
There wasn't even the faintest light inside or outside the car.
What on earth had happened?
I heard {n2} groan.
“{n2}? Are you okay?”
Only when I felt movement on top of my body did I realize she was lying on me.
From the force of the crash, we had both been flipped over.
What happened?”
“What do you mean what happened!{r}{p}Open that door and get out through the top.”
{n2} couldn't grasp the situation for a while, but eventually used me as a step to stretch up, opened the door, and climbed out.
She stepped on my face with a squish, but I gritted my teeth and bore it.
When {n2} jumped down, the car swayed unsteadily.
It's dangerous, so stay back!”
Calling that out, I climbed up to the door and jumped out.
The snow had turned into a full blizzard.
“What do we do...?”
I could hear {n2}'s voice, barely audible.
Thinking I mustn't show my anxiety here, I deliberately spoke in a cheerful voice.
“No help for it.
Let's walk.{r}{p}There might be a house along the way, and someone might pass by in a car.”
Luckily, the car had a powerful flashlight on board, probably for situations like this.
When I turned on the light, I jokingly lit my face from below.
“Kyaa!”
{n2} was more startled than I'd expected, which startled me too.
“Your face...
it's covered in blood.”
“Huh?”
When I gently touched it with my hand, sure enough, blood came away.
Apparently I'd cut my forehead on glass or something in the accident.
Once I noticed, it began to throb with heat.
“I'm fine.
Just a scratch.{r}{p}Come on, let's go.”
The circle lit by the flashlight was far too feeble and small.
The shrill wind shook the surrounding trees and froze my bare nose and ears.
The freezing air brought a piercing pain not only to my nasal membranes but deep into my lungs.
{n2} and I naturally held hands and started walking.
“Where
are we?”
{n2} said, wheezing.
“Huh?
Don't you know better than me?”
I asked back in surprise.
“But {n1} was always the one driving...”
Suddenly I started to lose confidence.
Could we really follow the right road in this darkness?
New snow began to pile up over the hard, slippery snow, and it started to crunch underfoot.
In the darkness there wasn't a sign of a car, much less a living thing, only the howl of the wind.
Whipping my heart, which was on the verge of despair, I just kept walking.
My boots sank into the snow up to the ankles and walking became harder.
If you gathered the snow clinging to my boots and clothes, it would probably weigh a considerable amount.
“Look!
A light!”
{n2} gripped my arm tightly.
Peering through the raging snow, I saw a faintly flickering light between the trees.
Faint as it was, it had to be the light of a building.
I pulled my feet, which had turned into pillars of ice, out of snow up to the knees and carried them forward.
Then the other foot.
Whipping my body, which seemed unable to move anymore, I advanced toward the light.
What if it's just a streetlight or something...
I shook that awful thought out of my head.
That's “Spur.”
It has to be.
It's about time we got there.
Once we got there, Mr. Kobayashi and his wife would welcome us and surely prepare a hot meal.
I tripped in the snow many times, but paid it no mind, got up, and kept walking.
The light gradually grew bigger.
No doubt.
That's “Spur.”
“...We're saved.”
{n2} murmured, sniffling.
“Yeah.”
I couldn't believe my luck.
Winning the lottery might feel like this.
But thinking about it, it wasn't luck at all.
To have suffered like this, you could even call it bad luck.
Anyway, before my eyes was the warm shelter I'd thought we'd never reach.
There'd be food, too.
Saved.
We were saved.
Thinking so, I felt happy from the bottom of my heart.
Summoning our last strength, we headed for the entrance porch.
...It felt strange.
But I had no leeway to stop and examine that unease.
All I wanted was to tumble into a warm room quickly and get some hot cocoa or soup...{r}{p}With that single thought I pushed desperately forward.
“Wait! {n1}!
What is... that?”
{n2} tugged my clothes from behind and pointed at the entrance.
“Huh?
What's that...?!”
I gasped.
Someone was lying at the entrance!
Could they have wandered lost just like us and collapsed from exhaustion there...?
But as we approached, I could tell the figure was still in indoor clothes.
Which meant it was a guest or one of the staff of “Spur.”
I climbed the porch steps and slowly approached the figure.
“Toshio...!”
The one lying slumped against the door was the part-timer, Toshio.
What shocked me even more was the dark blood flowing from his head.
I hurried over, grabbed Toshio's shoulders, and shook him.
“Toshio!
Toshio!”
From the instant I touched him I knew he couldn't be alive.
Snow had piled all over his body, and his clothes were even frozen.
Even if he'd been asleep, he'd have frozen to death long ago.
“Is he...
dead?”
I silently nodded at {n2}'s words.
“But why...?”
“Anyway, let's go inside.”
When I tried to open the door, I noticed the glass was broken.
The lock was still engaged.
It seemed Toshio had forcibly smashed the glass to try to open the door.
What on earth did this mean?
When I pressed the intercom button at the side, a chime rang out inside.
We waited a while, but no one came out.
Left with no choice, I reached through the broken glass, undid the lock, and went in.
“Did something...
happen?”
“...Yeah.
Maybe so...{r}{p}Anyone!
Is anyone there?
Mr. Kobayashi?”
I called out loudly, but there was no reply.
“For now, let's go back to our rooms and do something about these clothes.{r}{p}Otherwise we'll freeze to death too.”
I suggested that and started up the stairs.
But then I found something unbelievable yet again.
A woman was lying in the hallway.
A pool of black blood had formed around her head, and she didn't move.
“Kyaa!”
Keeping a tight grip on {n2}'s hand, I approached the woman.
It was Mrs. Kayama.
I put my hand to the neck of her where she lay on her back.
She was so cold I pulled my hand away without thinking.
“She's dead...”
“What...
what is going on?”
{n2} said in a feeble voice.
We had come seeking help, and a new nightmare was waiting for us here...
Shown such a thing at the end of a stream of tension and anxiety, my head fell into paralysis.
“M-Mr. Kobayashi! Mrs. Kobayashi! Anybody! Isn't anyone there?!”
I shouted desperately.
My voice was hoarse with fear, but I had no room to put up a front in front of {n2}.
“Anybody!”
All that came back was a terrifying silence.
I even thought of turning on my heel and going back out into the blizzard.
I didn't want to be here.
Something evil filled this place.
My emotions demanded I run, but reason held them down.
“Let's go to the Kobayashis' room.”
We crept down the stairs and headed for their room.
I'm scared.”
Earlier we'd been trembling from the cold; now we were trembling from fear.
We couldn't stop our teeth from chattering.
“Don't let go of me.”
I naturally lowered my voice.
What if someone was holding their breath, watching us...
Thinking so, I strained my ears, but all I heard was faint creaking floorboards and the wind outside.
Before long we reached the Kobayashis' room.
“...I don't want to go in.”
{n2} shook her head as if refusing.
“Then wait here.{r}{p}If anything happens, shout right away.”
Having said that, I peered through the door.
Mr. Kobayashi was sitting on the floor with his back against the wall and his legs stretched out.
A kitchen knife was stuck in his belly, and the area had turned into a sea of blood.
Nauseated, I covered my mouth with my hand and tried to dash into the bathroom.
But bright red blood was splattered in there too.
Mrs. Kobayashi, naked, had her head resting on the rim of the bathtub and stared at me with vacant eyes.
“Waaaaaah!”
I tumbled out of the room.
M-
M-
Mr. Kobayashi too...
Mr. Kobayashi too!”
I couldn't form words.
But {n2} seemed to grasp the situation.
“Everyone...
everyone was killed? By whom?”
“P-police,
call the police!”
I pulled {n2}'s hand and ran to the front desk.
I picked up the receiver and tried to dial 110.
Pressing the receiver to my ear and waiting, I realized after a while that there was no sound at all.
I pressed the hook switch over and over, but nothing changed.
“No good.
The line's dead.”
As I said it, I saw despair surface in {n2}'s big eyes.
“Why...
why?
What on earth is going on?!”
{n2} began to scream hysterically.
I felt like screaming too.
But looking at {n2}, I felt that I at least had to stay calm.
{r}...calm down.{r}{p}Let's go to the room.
We'll warm up and wait until morning.”
Something glistened down {n2}'s cheek.
“...Who
...who did something this terrible?{r}{p}Who would do such a horrible thing...”
“I don't know.{r}{p}It might be a burglar, or someone insane.{r}{p}I think he's probably not here anymore, but just in case, we have to protect ourselves somehow.”
{n2} might only now have been starting to grieve for her uncle's death.
Or perhaps fear beyond all limits had shredded her nerves.
{n2} hiccuped so hard she could hardly breathe, her whole face a mess of tears.
I pulled her close and gently held her shoulders.
“Pull yourself together.
Come on, let's go to the room.”
Supporting {n2}'s back, we headed to the second floor.
Trying not to look at the fallen Mrs. Kayama, I opened the door of my room.
I quickly scanned the room, but nothing was wrong.
No one seemed to be there.
Just to be sure, I looked into the bathroom too.
Nothing.
When I locked the door firmly, a wave of relief washed over me and I collapsed onto the bed.
“...Is this
...not a dream?
Isn't it a bad dream?{r}{p}Hey, {n1},
...tell me it's a dream.”
“It's okay.
I don't know what happened, but we were saved because we were late.{r}{p}By morning...”
Just then, a scream that shook the entire building rang out and froze our spines.
It was a woman's scream.
Someone was still alive...
But had that someone also just been killed by the killer's hand?
Unconsciously, {n2} and I held each other tightly.
Another woman's scream came, and I felt {n2}'s body jolt.
Then, a silence so intense it hurt my ears.
...And then I heard faint creaking of the floor.
Someone was walking down the hallway.
Slowly, slowly approaching us.
I gripped {n2}'s hand.
It's all right.
No one should know that {n2} and I are here...
probably.
The footsteps stopped outside the door.
I worried that the sound of me swallowing might be heard outside.
